topic: Moray eels have a second set of jaws
script: Moray eels have a second set of jaws inside their throat. After the front jaws grab prey, the inner jaws shoot forward. They clamp on and drag the prey down into the throat. Scientists described how this works in 2007. Morays are fish, even though they look like snakes. They often open and close their mouths to pump water over their gills, which is breathing, not a threat. Follow Pixel Abyss for more strange facts from the deep.
